name: Cathedral Range State Park

facts.claim: Jagged ridges of the Cathedral Range offer views and some of the best hiking in Victoria
Walks range from the gentle Friends Nature Trail to the hard Razorback Trail and Sugarloaf Peak (920 m)
Camping at Cooks Mill and The Farmyard hike-in area; kangaroos and lyrebirds live in the park

name: South Jawbone Peak

facts.claim: South Jawbone Peak Walk is a marked track in Cathedral Range State Park
Steep track with uneven ground; Parks Victoria warns of snakes and terrain hazards
Dogs, bicycles and horses are not allowed

name: Beeches Rainforest Walk

facts.claim: Rainforest walk in Yarra Ranges National Park through Myrtle Beech and Mountain Ash forest, lyrebirds often heard
Starts at Taggerty Cascades car park off Lady Talbot Drive near Marysville; about 3.4-4 km loop (sources vary)
Picnic tables and toilets at nearby The Beeches Picnic Area; no dogs; limbs may fall

unresolved: Length conflicts between sources (3.4 vs 4 km)

name: Ada Tree

facts.claim: Giant Mountain Ash in Yarra State Forest near Powelltown, over 300 years old and about 76 m tall (figures vary)
Short easy walk of about 3.2 km return from the car park and picnic area, with wheelchair-accessible boardwalk
Reached by gravel road from Warburton, Powelltown or Noojee; picnic shelter and toilets on site

name: O'Shannassy Aqueduct Trail

facts.claim: Historic aqueduct trail through Yarra Ranges National Park from Don Valley to East Warburton
Roughly 30-34 km one way depending on source; shared by walkers and cyclists
Parks Victoria restricts night-time access along the trail due to deer control

facts.claim: Park on the slopes of the Great Dividing Range with views to Melbourne, Port Phillip Bay and the Yarra Valley
Masons Falls: short walk to water cascading over mudstone walls, with picnic area and free gas barbecues
Mount Sugarloaf lookout and Bowden Spur mountain bike trail; 232 km2 park
